facts.statement: The researchers used a rat model specifically designed to show post-stroke headache symptoms like sensitivity to orbital pressure and excessive face grooming.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Giving rats different amounts of gastrodin reduced their pain-related behaviors in a way that depended on the dose given.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: When the rats were treated with a drug that blocks the PI3K pathway, the pain relief and brain protection caused by gastrodin disappeared.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The study included 80 people who had had an acute ischemic stroke and 50 healthy people for comparison.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: In the human patients, lower levels of PI3K and Akt proteins in the blood were linked to more severe headaches and worse neurological outcomes.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Gastrodin treatment increased the activity of the PI3K/Akt pathway in the brain area surrounding the stroke, which was shown by higher levels of specific proteins.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The authors note that post-stroke headaches and other neurological problems make the overall recovery from stroke much worse.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Before this research, it was not known if gastrodin could stop post-stroke headaches or how it worked to do so.
facts.subject: humans
